dedupe_keys.name: unified 0 25 degree gridded infrastructure critical extreme weather for the united states from 1979 to 2100

description: Unified 0.25-degree gridded infrastructure-critical extreme weather for the United States from 1979 to 2100 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Tao Sun et al. Extreme weather events can severely disrupt critical infrastructure, triggering cascading effects on power, transportation, and essential services. However, standard weather and climate datasets often lack specialized variables necessary for hazard assessments. We present a unified dataset of infrastructure-critical weather and climate variables across the United States at 0.25° resolution, covering daily or sub-daily intervals from 1979 to 2100. Coverage: national (US); published in 2025. Formats: NetCDF. The data are held in Jülich DATA and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
